sections.html:
Sherwood belongs to Pulaski County and the Little Rock-North Little Rock-Conway metro. Its ZIP code is 72120, and Arkansas Highway 107 cuts through town. The city grew from 21,511 people in 2000 to 32,731 in 2020, and 33,620 are estimated for 2025. Annexing the old Gravel Ridge area in 2008 supplied the city's first and second wards.

This is mostly a town of owner-occupied houses, as the numbers below show.

Housing measureSherwood, 2020 to 2024
Owner-occupied housing rate70.8%
Median value, owner-occupied homes$199,500
Median gross rent$1,101
Households14,077

Because owners outnumber renters by a wide margin, the typical seller here is a homeowner rather than a landlord, and the condition of the roof and systems tends to decide price.

sections.h2: The March 2023 tornado and your house
sections.html:
An EF3 tornado with estimated peak winds of 165 mph struck on March 31, 2023. Its path ran northeast through Sherwood, mostly along Lee Avenue, and many homes were damaged. It carried on toward Kiehl Avenue, where more homes and a few businesses near Northgate Drive and Woodridge Lane were hit. The storm stayed down for 34.4 miles and grew as wide as 600 yards.

A house near that path may carry storm history. Expect three topics when it goes up for sale:

  • Quick roof and decking repairs after the storm may have no permit or final inspection on file.
  • Buyers and lenders ask for the insurance claim file, contractor invoices and warranties, so keep them in one folder.
  • Half-finished repairs make a conventional mortgage hard to get, and that pushes some owners toward an as-is sale.

sections.h2: Heat, moisture and what buyers check
sections.html:
Summers are hot and winters mild, with roughly 50 inches of rain a year and July highs that average 92 degrees. Long cooling seasons wear out air conditioners, and roofs absorb sun and storms. An inspector walking a Sherwood house will look first at the roof, the HVAC unit and any trace of water intrusion.

When all three are aging, fixing them before you list may cost more than it returns. A cash buyer builds the repairs into the offer and takes the house as it stands.

One district, the Pulaski County Special School District, covers all of Sherwood, Gravel Ridge included. Sylvan Hills High School is the public high school, with Sylvan Hills Middle School alongside four elementary schools in the city: Clinton Speech Communications and Technology Magnet, Oakbrooke, Sherwood and Sylvan Hills. LISA Academy North is a public charter option.

Buyers place a house faster when the school zone is named, so note it in your listing details or your first talk with a buyer.

Call the Permits and Planning staff at 501-835-4753 on weekdays, 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., for anything about building permits. Online, the city offers a permits portal and downloadable forms for residential building, electrical and plumbing work.

Did a deck, an addition or a post-tornado roof go in without a permit? Ask the office what a late permit would involve before you sign a contract, because a buyer's inspector often notices the gap.

Common seller tasks in Sherwood:

  • Request the permit history for structural, electrical or plumbing work.
  • Make sure city utilities are still active.
  • Look up the parcel at the Pulaski County assessor and check the owner name and mailing address.
  • Find the deed, plus the court papers that let you sign if the house was inherited.

A Sherwood house is taxed by the county, the school district and the city, and the bill falls due October 15. Values are reset every three, four or five years. When a number looks wrong, call the county assessor first, because mistakes in the property description can often be corrected without a formal appeal. To go further, request a county Board of Equalization hearing by the third Monday in August.

Increases are capped at up to 5 percent a year for owner-occupied homes and up to 10 percent for rentals. Owners 65 or older, and disabled owners, may ask the assessor to freeze the assessed value. A mid-year sale raises the question of who owes what, so ask the title company how the current year's tax will be divided at closing.

Deeds and similar instruments carry Arkansas's real property transfer tax, $3.30 per $1,000 of the actual consideration. Say in the contract who pays, and check it with the closing agent.

The fee is small beside a commission or a repair bill, but each path to closing has its own line items. Ask for a written cash offer that lists them all, so you can see what you would net.

sections.h2: Preparing to sell after storm damage or repairs
sections.html:
Start with a folder. Put in it the insurance claim, the contractor invoices, any warranty papers and photos taken before and after the work. Then ask the permit office whether each repair has a permit that was closed out. A buyer's inspector sees the roof from the street, and open permits turn into questions at the closing table.

If repairs are only half done, decide whether you will finish them. Finishing means paying contractors and waiting. Selling as-is means the buyer takes over the unfinished work and the price reflects it. Neither choice is wrong, but you should compare both with real numbers.

The title company confirms who owns the house, finds any lien or unpaid tax, and prepares the closing statement. Your mortgage payoff and any balance owed to the county come out of the proceeds. You sign the deed, and the transfer tax and recording are handled as part of the closing.

If the house was inherited, bring the court papers that show your authority to sign. If it is rented, bring the lease and the tenant's contact details so the buyer knows what to expect.

sections.h2: When a cash sale makes sense
sections.html:
A cash sale tends to fit when the house needs repairs a lender would not accept, when you want a firm closing date, or when the property came through probate. A conventional listing can still bring a higher price on a house in good shape, so ask an agent for an opinion before you decide.

Cash Home Buyers buys houses as-is across Arkansas. You can compare its offer with a listing estimate and choose.

Whichever way you lean, ask each buyer or agent what you would pay out of pocket and what you would receive, and ask when the money arrives. A written answer to those three questions makes the comparison honest. Mention any storm damage, open permits or tenants at the start so the number you get is a number that holds.

faqs.q: How many people live in Sherwood, Arkansas?
faqs.a: An estimated 33,620 as of July 1, 2025. The 2020 count was 32,731 and the 2000 count was 21,511.
Yes. The EF3 tornado of March 31, 2023 moved northeast through Sherwood generally along Lee Avenue and damaged many homes, then continued toward Kiehl Avenue.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Arkansas?
faqs.a: October 15 each year. Late real estate payments carry penalties and interest, so confirm the current amount with the county collector.

faqs.q: What does the Arkansas transfer tax cost?
faqs.a: It is $3.30 per $1,000 of the sale price on a deed. Agree in the contract who pays it.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Sherwood house that needs a new roof?
faqs.a: Yes. Buyers who pay cash often purchase houses as-is, so roofing, HVAC and storm repairs do not have to be finished before closing.
